questions.text: All of the following are contents of sup mediastinum except:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) because the ascending aorta lies in the middle mediastinum within the pericardium, not in the superior mediastinum. The arch of the aorta, the left brachiocephalic vein and both vagus nerves are all classical contents of the superior mediastinum.
questions.keyConcept: The ascending aorta belongs to the middle mediastinum; the aortic arch belongs to the superior mediastinum.

questions.text: Which of the following structures doesn't pass through the Aortic opening of Diaphragm?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (D) because the right phrenic nerve pierces the diaphragm through the vena caval opening at T8, alongside the inferior vena cava. The aortic opening at T12 transmits the descending thoracic aorta, the thoracic duct and the azygos vein.
questions.keyConcept: Aortic opening (T12): aorta, thoracic duct, azygos vein. The right phrenic nerve uses the vena caval opening.

questions.text: Azygous vein ends in which of the following vein?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because the azygos vein arches over the root of the right lung and drains into the superior vena cava. It does not join the inferior vena cava, a brachiocephalic vein or the subclavian vein, although it does form an important collateral channel between the caval systems.
questions.keyConcept: The azygos vein ends in the superior vena cava and links the caval systems.

questions.text: Apex of the heart is formed by:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because the apex of the heart is formed by the left ventricle and lies in the left fifth intercostal space just medial to the midclavicular line. The right ventricle forms most of the sternocostal surface, while the atria lie at the base of the heart.
questions.keyConcept: The apex of the heart is formed by the left ventricle.

questions.text: Upper border of the heart is formed by:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) because the upper border of the heart is formed by the two atria, mainly the left atrium and its auricle, which lie most superiorly and posteriorly. The ventricles form the inferior and sternocostal parts of the heart rather than its upper border.
questions.keyConcept: The upper border of the heart is formed by the atria, chiefly the left atrium.

questions.text: Sternocostal surface of the heart is formed mainly by:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because the right ventricle forms the greater part of the sternocostal (anterior) surface of the heart, which is why it is the chamber most often injured in penetrating anterior chest wounds. The right atrium contributes to the right of this surface and the left ventricle only a narrow strip on the left.
questions.keyConcept: The right ventricle forms most of the sternocostal surface of the heart.

questions.text: All of the following structures seen on the base of the heart except:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) because the left ventricle does not appear on the base of the heart, which is formed mainly by the left atrium receiving the four pulmonary veins, with a small contribution from the right atrium. The base faces posteriorly towards the vertebral column.
questions.keyConcept: The base of the heart is formed mainly by the left atrium and the pulmonary veins.

questions.text: Thoracic duct receives lymph from all the following except:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because lymph from the right upper limb drains through the right lymphatic duct, not the thoracic duct. The thoracic duct drains both lower limbs, the pelvis and abdomen, the left half of the thorax, the left upper limb and the left side of the head and neck.
questions.keyConcept: The thoracic duct drains everything except the right upper limb and the right side of the head, neck and thorax.

questions.text: Thoracic duct end in which of the following?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) because the thoracic duct ends by opening into the beginning of the left brachiocephalic vein, at the junction of the left subclavian and left internal jugular veins. It has no connection with the right brachiocephalic vein, the superior vena cava or the inferior vena cava.
questions.keyConcept: The thoracic duct ends at the junction of the left subclavian and left internal jugular veins.

questions.text: The arteries that supplying the heart muscle are branches of:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) because the right and left coronary arteries arise from the ascending aorta, just above the aortic valve in the right and left aortic sinuses. The arch of the aorta gives the three great vessels of the head, neck and upper limbs instead.
questions.keyConcept: The coronary arteries arise from the aortic sinuses of the ascending aorta.

questions.text: All are true about sterna angle except:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) because the ascending aorta begins lower down, at the aortic valve behind the third costal cartilage, and not at the sternal angle. The sternal angle lies opposite the second costal cartilages and the T4/T5 disc, and marks the bifurcation of the trachea and the end of the ascending aorta where the arch begins.
questions.keyConcept: The sternal angle (T4/T5, 2nd costal cartilage) marks tracheal bifurcation and the end of the ascending aorta.
options: Opposite to the disc between T4, T5.

questions.text: The coronary sinus (vein of the heart) ends in:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (D) because the coronary sinus, which collects most of the venous blood of the heart, opens into the right atrium between the opening of the inferior vena cava and the atrioventricular orifice. It does not drain into the caval veins or the brachiocephalic vein.
questions.keyConcept: The coronary sinus opens into the right atrium, guarded by a semicircular valve.

questions.text: All are true about esophageal opening of diaphragm except:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (A) because the phrenic nerve does not use the oesophageal opening: the right phrenic passes through the vena caval opening and the left phrenic pierces the muscular dome directly. The oesophageal opening lies at T10, about an inch to the left of the median plane, and transmits the oesophagus with both vagi and the oesophageal branches of the left gastric vessels.
questions.keyConcept: Oesophageal opening (T10): oesophagus, both vagi and left gastric oesophageal branches.
options: Opposite to level of 10th thoracic vertebra.
Located 1 inch lt to median plane.

questions.text: Neuro vascular plane of thorax lies between:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because the intercostal nerve and vessels run in the plane between the internal intercostal and the innermost intercostal muscles, sheltered in the subcostal groove. This is the plane entered deliberately during intercostal nerve block and avoided during chest drain insertion.
questions.keyConcept: The thoracic neurovascular plane lies between the internal and innermost intercostal muscles.

questions.text: The intercostal nerves are:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (D) because the intercostal nerves are the ventral rami of the first eleven thoracic spinal nerves; the ventral ramus of T12 lies below the twelfth rib and is named the subcostal nerve. Options (a) and (b) are wrong because a ventral root is a component of the spinal nerve itself, not a named peripheral nerve.
questions.keyConcept: Intercostal nerves = ventral rami of T1–T11; the T12 ventral ramus is the subcostal nerve.

questions.text: All are the contents of middle mediastinum except:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (D) because the right vagus nerve descends through the superior and then the posterior mediastinum and is not a content of the middle mediastinum. The middle mediastinum contains the heart and pericardium, the ascending aorta, the pulmonary trunk, the pulmonary veins, the lower half of the superior vena cava and the phrenic nerves.
questions.keyConcept: Middle mediastinum: heart and pericardium, ascending aorta, pulmonary trunk and veins, lower SVC, phrenic nerves.

questions.text: As regards the thoracic cage, choose the INCORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The sternal angle is the junction between the manubrium and the body of the sternum; the junction with the xiphoid process is the xiphisternal joint.
questions.keyConcept: The sternal angle is the manubriosternal junction, not the xiphisternal junction.
options: It is formed of sternum anteriorly.
It is formed posteriorly by thoracic vertebrae.
The junction between body and xiphoid process is called sternal angle.
The ribs form the lateral part of the thoracic cage.

questions.text: Sternal angle lies opposite the disc between:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is T4 & T5. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: The correct answer is T4 & T5. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification

questions.text: Which ribs attach to the sternum indirectly through the costal cartilage of the rib above?
questions.explanation: Ribs 8–10 attach indirectly through adjoining costal cartilage. Ribs 11–12 are floating ribs without an anterior sternal connection; the broader false-rib category includes ribs 8–12.
questions.keyConcept: 8th, 9th & 10th ribs

questions.text: The ribs that have no anterior attachment are:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Lower 2 ribs. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: Lower 2 ribs

questions.text: Each vertebra has all the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 2 spines. The remaining options describe the normal anatomy correctly.
questions.keyConcept: The correct answer is 2 spines. The remaining options describe the normal anatomy correctly

questions.text: Diaphragm takes origin from all the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Lower 8 ribs. The remaining options describe the normal anatomy correctly.
questions.keyConcept: Lower 8 ribs

questions.text: Crura of diaphragm are attached to:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Bodies of lumbar vertebrae. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: Bodies of lumbar vertebrae

questions.text: Caval opening of diaphragm lies at the level of:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is T8. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: The correct answer is T8. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification

questions.text: Vagi pass in diaphragm through:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Esophageal opening. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: Esophageal opening

questions.text: Esophageal opening of diaphragm transmits:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Esophagus & vagi. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: Esophagus & vagi

questions.text: As regards the diaphragm, choose the CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The diaphragm arises from the xiphoid process, the inner surfaces of the lower six costal cartilages and adjacent ribs, and the lumbar crura, so origin from the lower six ribs is the correct statement here.
questions.keyConcept: The diaphragm takes costal origin from the lower six ribs and their costal cartilages.
options: It takes origin from lower 6 ribs.
It is inserted into arcuate ligaments.
Its aortic opening transmits the vagi.
Its esophageal opening lies at level of T8.

questions.text: Each intercostal space contains:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is One large posterior intercostal artery. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: One large posterior intercostal artery
options: Posterior ramus of a thoracic spinal nerve

questions.text: A typical intercostal space among the upper nine contains all the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Posterior ramus of a thoracic spinal nerve. The remaining options describe the normal anatomy correctly.
questions.keyConcept: Posterior ramus of a thoracic spinal nerve
options: Posterior ramus of a thoracic spinal nerve

questions.text: Boundaries of mediastinum include all the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Ribs. The remaining options describe the normal anatomy correctly.
questions.keyConcept: The correct answer is Ribs. The remaining options describe the normal anatomy correctly

questions.text: Match each structure with its relation to the mediastinum:
questions.explanation: Each structure is matched to its standard anatomical relation or compartment.
questions.keyConcept: Know the defining relations and compartments of thoracic structures.

questions.text: As regards the middle mediastinum, choose the CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The middle mediastinum contains the pericardium and heart, together with the roots of the great vessels. The other options describe boundaries or neighboring compartments rather than its main content.
questions.keyConcept: The heart lies in the middle mediastinum within the pericardium.
options: It lies above an imaginary line at level of sternal angle.
It lies below a line at level of T6 vertebra.
It lies between heart & vertebral column.

questions.text: Posterior mediastinum is bounded by all the following structures EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Sternum. The remaining options describe the normal anatomy correctly.
questions.keyConcept: The correct answer is Sternum. The remaining options describe the normal anatomy correctly
options: Imaginary line at level of sternal angle

questions.text: Which of the following DOES NOT share in the walls of the anterior mediastinum?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Vertebral column. The remaining options describe the normal anatomy correctly.
questions.keyConcept: Vertebral column
options: Imaginary line at level of T4

questions.text: Superior mediastinum is bounded by all the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Heart. The remaining options describe the normal anatomy correctly.
questions.keyConcept: The correct answer is Heart. The remaining options describe the normal anatomy correctly
options: Imaginary line between sternal angle & T4

questions.text: The structure that lies in anterior & superior mediastinum is:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Thymus. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: The correct answer is Thymus. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification

questions.text: Match each structure with its mediastinal location:
questions.explanation: The ascending aorta lies within the pericardium in the middle mediastinum. The arch of the aorta lies in the superior mediastinum, the descending thoracic aorta lies in the posterior mediastinum, the thymus occupies the superior mediastinum and may extend into the anterior mediastinum, and the esophagus passes through the superior and posterior mediastina.
questions.keyConcept: Arch of aorta = superior mediastinum; descending aorta = posterior mediastinum; ascending aorta = middle mediastinum.

questions.text: As regards superior vena cava, choose the CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The superior vena cava is formed by the union of the right and left brachiocephalic veins in the superior mediastinum, then descends to open into the right atrium.
questions.keyConcept: The superior vena cava is formed in the superior mediastinum by the brachiocephalic veins.
options: It is formed in superior mediastinum.
It is the continuation of the left brachiocephalic vein.
Right brachiocephalic vein ends in its middle.

questions.text: As regards azygos vein, choose the CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The azygos vein arches over the root of the right lung and opens into the posterior aspect of the superior vena cava. It does not end in the inferior vena cava or run in the anterior mediastinum.
questions.keyConcept: The azygos vein arches over the right lung root to join the superior vena cava posteriorly.
options: It is formed by union of right & left brachiocephalic veins.
It ends in inferior vena cava.
It enters thorax through caval opening of diaphragm.
It opens in back of superior vena cava.

questions.text: As regards ascending aorta, choose the CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The ascending aorta begins at the left ventricle and lies within the fibrous pericardium before continuing as the arch of the aorta.
questions.keyConcept: The ascending aorta is intrapericardial and arises from the left ventricle.

questions.text: As regards arch of aorta, choose the INCORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The arch of the aorta belongs to the superior mediastinum, not the middle mediastinum. It continues from the ascending aorta and gives the brachiocephalic, left common carotid, and left subclavian arteries.
questions.keyConcept: The arch of the aorta lies in the superior mediastinum.
options: It is the continuation of ascending aorta.
It gives left common carotid & left subclavian artery.
Its branches leave thorax through superior aperture.

questions.text: As regards descending aorta, choose the CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The descending thoracic aorta passes through the aortic hiatus of the diaphragm to become the abdominal aorta. It is not within the pericardium and does not give the brachiocephalic artery.
questions.keyConcept: The descending thoracic aorta enters the abdomen through the aortic hiatus.
options: It runs in superior & posterior mediastinum.
It is continuation of ascending aorta.
It passes through diaphragm to enter the abdomen.

questions.text: As regards the trachea, choose the CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The trachea begins at the level of C6, enters the thorax through the superior thoracic aperture, and descends to bifurcate near the sternal angle.
questions.keyConcept: The trachea passes through the superior thoracic aperture before bifurcating near the sternal angle.
options: It is a completely muscular tube.
It passes through superior thoracic aperture.
It begins at level of sternal angle.

questions.text: In superior mediastinum, the structures have the following arrangement from anterior to posterior:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Arch of aorta, trachea & esophagus. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: Arch of aorta, trachea & esophagus

questions.text: As regards esophagus, choose the INCORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The esophagus runs mainly in the posterior mediastinum after beginning in the neck, so describing it as a middle-mediastinal structure is the incorrect statement.
questions.keyConcept: The esophagus is mainly a posterior-mediastinal structure.
options: It passes in diaphragm at level of T10.

questions.text: As regards the thoracic duct, choose the CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The thoracic duct ascends in the posterior mediastinum behind the esophagus before entering the root of the neck. It does not end inside the thorax or drain into the right brachiocephalic vein.
questions.keyConcept: The thoracic duct ascends behind the esophagus in the posterior mediastinum.
options: It ascends through esophageal opening of diaphragm.
It ascends through middle & superior mediastinum.
It ends into right brachiocephalic vein.

questions.text: As regards the thoracic duct, choose the INCORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The thoracic duct usually ends at the left venous angle in the root of the neck, so drainage into the right brachiocephalic vein is the incorrect statement.
questions.keyConcept: The thoracic duct ends at the left venous angle, not the right brachiocephalic vein.
options: It ascends through aortic opening of diaphragm.
It ascends through posterior & superior mediastinum.
It ascends through superior thoracic aperture.
It ends into right brachiocephalic vein.

questions.text: As regards the vagi, choose the INCORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The vagus nerves pass through the diaphragm with the esophagus via the esophageal hiatus, not through the aortic hiatus.
questions.keyConcept: The vagus nerves pass through the esophageal hiatus with the esophagus.
options: They descend from neck to thorax.
They give parasympathetic supply to bronchi & heart.
They pass through aortic opening of diaphragm.
The left vagus gives left recurrent laryngeal nerve.

questions.text: The mediastinum contains all the following structures EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Right recurrent laryngeal nerve. The remaining options describe the normal anatomy correctly.
questions.keyConcept: Right recurrent laryngeal nerve

questions.text: As regards the phrenic nerves, choose the INCORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The phrenic nerves descend through the neck and superior mediastinum on either side of the pericardium; they are not posterior-mediastinal nerves.
questions.keyConcept: The phrenic nerves descend in the superior mediastinum along the pericardium.
options: They pass through superior thoracic aperture.
They descend in superior & posterior mediastinum.
They descend on sides of mediastinum.

questions.text: Match each structure with its containing mediastinum:
questions.explanation: Each structure is matched to its standard anatomical relation or compartment.
questions.keyConcept: Know the defining relations and compartments of thoracic structures.

questions.text: Match each structure with its mediastinal course:
questions.explanation: Each structure is matched to its standard anatomical relation or compartment.
questions.keyConcept: Know the defining relations and compartments of thoracic structures.

questions.text: As regards the pericardium, choose the INCORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The pericardial cavity contains a thin film of serous fluid and lies between the parietal and visceral layers of the serous pericardium; it is not between the fibrous and visceral pericardium.
questions.keyConcept: The pericardial cavity lies between the parietal and visceral serous pericardium.
options: It encloses roots of great vessels.
Its serous part is formed of 2 layers.
It has a cavity filled with fluid & it lies between fibrous & visceral pericardium.

questions.text: As regards the heart, choose the CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Its apex is directed to the left. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: Its apex is directed to the left.
options: Its apex is directed to the left.
Its diaphragmatic surface is to the right.
Its base is formed mainly by right atrium.

questions.text: As regards the heart, choose the INCORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The sternocostal surface of the heart is formed mainly by the right ventricle. The left ventricle contributes much of the left border and apex instead.
questions.keyConcept: The sternocostal surface of the heart is formed mainly by the right ventricle.
options: Its apex is formed by left ventricle.
Its base is formed by 2 atria.
Its sternocostal surface is formed mainly by left ventricle.
Atria in sternocostal surface are hidden behind ascending aorta & pulmonary artery.

questions.text: Match each cardiac border with the chamber(s) forming it:
questions.explanation: Each structure is matched to its standard anatomical relation or compartment.
questions.keyConcept: Know the defining relations and compartments of thoracic structures.

questions.text: As regards the coronary circulation, choose the CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Heart is supplied by 2 coronary arteries. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: Heart is supplied by 2 coronary arteries.
options: Heart is supplied by 2 coronary arteries.
Coronary arteries arise from aortic arch.
Right coronary artery gives marginal & anterior interventricular arteries.
Left coronary artery gives circumflex & posterior interventricular arteries.
Coronary sinus opens in left atrium.

questions.text: In the usual right-dominant coronary circulation, the posterior interventricular artery is a branch of which artery?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Right coronary artery. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: Right coronary artery

questions.text: As regards lung & pleura, choose the INCORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The pleura is a serous sac with parietal and visceral layers, separated by a potential pleural cavity. It is not a fibrous sac.
questions.keyConcept: Pleura is a serous sac, not a fibrous sac.
options: Pleural space lies between visceral & parietal pleura.
Pleura is invaginated by lung from medial surface.
Each lung has the shape of half a cone.
Each lung has an apex & a base.

questions.text: Left lung:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Has a cardiac notch. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: Has a cardiac notch

questions.text: As regards right lung, choose the INCORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The right lung has three lobes and two fissures, but it does not have a lingula. The lingula is a feature of the left upper lobe.
questions.keyConcept: The lingula belongs to the left lung, not the right lung.
options: It is shorter than left lung.
It is broader than left lung.

questions.text: The structure that supplies the lung tissue with oxygenated blood is:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Bronchial arteries. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: Bronchial arteries

questions.text: Pulmonary circulation includes the flow of blood from:
questions.explanation: Pulmonary circulation begins at the right ventricle and travels through the pulmonary trunk to the lungs.
questions.keyConcept: Pulmonary Circulation: Pulmonary circulation begins at the right ventricle and travels through the pulmonary trunk to the lungs
options: Left ventricle through aorta to body.
Right ventricle through pulmonary trunk to lungs.
Left atrium through left ventricle to aorta.
Left ventricle through aorta to lungs.
Right atrium through right ventricle to aorta.

questions.text: The manubriosternal joint is classified as:
questions.explanation: The manubriosternal joint is a secondary cartilaginous symphysis.
questions.keyConcept: Sternal Joints: The manubriosternal joint is a secondary cartilaginous symphysis

questions.text: Which part of the thoracic spinal nerve contains preganglionic sympathetic fibers?
questions.explanation: Preganglionic sympathetic fibers leave the spinal cord through ventral roots.
questions.keyConcept: Thoracic Spinal Nerves: Preganglionic sympathetic fibers leave the spinal cord through ventral roots

questions.text: Axial skeleton includes:
questions.explanation: The sternum belongs to the axial skeleton.
questions.keyConcept: Axial Skeleton: The sternum belongs to the axial skeleton

questions.text: An example of axial bone is:
questions.explanation: The sternum belongs to the axial skeleton.
questions.keyConcept: Axial skeleton

questions.text: Pleurae are serous membranes of the:
questions.explanation: Pleurae are the serous membranes associated with the lungs.
questions.keyConcept: Pleurae are the serous membranes associated with the lungs

questions.text: Regarding the Base of the heart, one is correct:
questions.explanation: The base of the heart is formed mainly by the left atrium, with a small contribution from the right atrium.
questions.keyConcept: Base of the heart
options: Forms the anterior surface of the heart.
Formed mainly by the left atrium and a small part by the right atrium.
Directed downwards, forwards and to the left.
Divided by the coronary groove into atrial portion above, and a ventricular portion below.

questions.text: Regarding the apex of the heart, one is correct:
questions.explanation: The apex beat is found in the left 5th intercostal space about 3.5 inches from the median plane.
questions.keyConcept: Apex of the heart
options: Forms the anterior surface of the heart.
Formed mainly by the left atrium.
Directed downwards, forwards and to the right.
Lies in the left 5th intercostal space, 3.5 inches from the median plane.

questions.text: Regarding the sternocostal surface of the heart, one is correct:
questions.explanation: The coronary groove separates the atrial portion above from the ventricular portion below on the sternocostal surface.
questions.keyConcept: Sternocostal surface
options: Divided by the coronary groove into atrial portion above, and a ventricular portion below.
Formed mainly by the left atrium.
It is divided equally into right and left halves.

questions.text: Regarding the borders of the heart, one is correct:
questions.explanation: The right border of the heart is formed mainly by the right atrium.
questions.keyConcept: Right cardiac border
options: Inferior border formed by left ventricle (mainly).
Left border formed by right ventricle (mainly).
Superior border formed by right atrium (mainly).
Right border formed by the right atrium.

questions.text: Regarding the chambers of the heart, one is correct:
questions.explanation: Blood flows from the right atrium through the right atrioventricular orifice into the right ventricle.
questions.keyConcept: Right atrioventricular flow
options: The Right Atrium receives oxygenated blood by the way of the superior and inferior vena cava.
From the Right Atrium, the blood passes through the right atrioventricular orifice into the Right Ventricle.
Contraction of Right Ventricle forces the blood to pass through the aorta to the lungs.
The right atrioventricular orifice is guarded by mitral valve.
The orifice of pulmonary artery is guarded by tricuspid valve.

questions.text: Which of the following arteries is a branch from the arch of the aorta?
questions.explanation: The left subclavian artery is a direct branch of the arch of the aorta.
questions.keyConcept: The arch of the aorta gives the left subclavian artery directly.

questions.text: Which of the following arteries is a branch from the ascending aorta?
questions.explanation: The coronary arteries arise from the ascending aorta at the aortic sinuses.
questions.keyConcept: The left coronary artery is a branch of the ascending aorta.

questions.text: Which of the following veins ends in the right atrium?
questions.explanation: The superior vena cava opens directly into the right atrium.
questions.keyConcept: The superior vena cava drains into the right atrium.

questions.text: Normally, the esophagus shows constrictions at the following sites, except:
questions.explanation: The thoracic duct does not form one of the normal oesophageal constrictions.
questions.keyConcept: Normal oesophageal constrictions do not include the thoracic duct crossing.
options: Where it is crossed by the arch of aorta.
Where it is crossed by the left bronchus.
Where it is crossed by the thoracic duct.

questions.text: Regarding the trachea one of the following statements is true:
questions.explanation: The trachea begins as a continuation of the larynx at the level of C6.
questions.keyConcept: The trachea starts at C6.
options: It starts as a continuation of larynx at the level of C6.
It is separated from the vertebral Column it by the pharynx.
It is related anteriorly to the oesophagus.
It is composed of four incomplete C shaped rings of hyaline cartilage.
It is related laterally, in its upper part to the lungs.

questions.text: Regarding the bronchi one of the following statements is true:
questions.explanation: The right main bronchus divides into three lobar bronchi for the three lobes of the right lung.
questions.keyConcept: The right main bronchus divides into three lobar bronchi.
options: Right bronchus is longer than Left bronchus.
Left bronchus is wider than Right bronchus.
Left bronchus is more vertical nearly in line with trachea.

questions.text: Thoracic cage is formed of ___ anterior and ___ in each side.
questions.explanation: The sternum forms the anterior part of the thoracic cage and ribs lie on each side.
questions.keyConcept: The thoracic cage consists of sternum anteriorly and ribs laterally.

questions.text: The true ribs are ___ pairs in number, while the floating ribs are ___ pairs in number.
questions.explanation: There are 7 pairs of true ribs and 2 pairs of floating ribs.
questions.keyConcept: There are 7 true ribs and 2 floating ribs.

questions.text: The esophagus is about ___ cm in length and show ___ constrictions.
questions.explanation: The oesophagus is about 25 cm long and has four normal constrictions.
questions.keyConcept: The oesophagus is about 25 cm long with four constrictions.

questions.text: Trachea starts at the level of ___ and ends at the level of ___.
questions.explanation: The trachea begins at C6 and bifurcates around the T4 level.
questions.keyConcept: The trachea extends from C6 to about T4.

questions.text: The ___ bronchus is shorter than the ___ bronchus.
questions.explanation: The right main bronchus is shorter, wider, and more vertical than the left.
questions.keyConcept: The right main bronchus is shorter than the left.

questions.text: The right lung divides into ___ lobes while the left lung divides into ___ lobes.
questions.explanation: The right lung has three lobes and the left lung has two.
questions.keyConcept: Right lung has three lobes; left lung has two.

questions.text: Esophageal opening of diaphragm:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (A) because the oesophageal opening lies at the level of the 10th thoracic vertebra, giving the useful mnemonic that the oesophagus passes at T10. Option (b) is wrong because it lies within the fibers of the right crus, and (c) is wrong because those fibers act as a physiological sphincter that narrows the opening on contraction. Option (d) is wrong because it lies about an inch to the left of the midline, and (e) is wrong because the caval opening, not the oesophageal, lies in the central tendon.
questions.keyConcept: The oesophageal opening of the diaphragm lies at T10, within the right crus, just left of the midline.
options: Lies within left crus of diaphragm.
Its diameter is not affected by contraction of diaphragm.
It lies 1 inch to the right of midline.

questions.text: Aortic opening of diaphragm lies:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) because the aortic opening lies in the midline at the level of the 12th thoracic vertebra, behind the median arcuate ligament. It is the oesophageal opening at T10 that is displaced to the left of the midline (b), and the caval opening lies at T8 (d) to the right. Options (a) and (e) give the correct vertebral level but wrongly displace the opening from the midline.
questions.keyConcept: The aortic opening of the diaphragm is a midline opening at the level of T12.
options: At level of T12, one inch to left of midline.
At level of T10, one inch to left of midline.
At level of T12 in midline.
At level of T8 in midline.
At level of T12, one inch to right of midline.

questions.text: Aortic opening of the diaphragm:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because the aortic opening is an osseoaponeurotic hiatus lying behind the median arcuate ligament, which arches between the two crura. Because the aorta passes behind rather than through muscle fibers, its diameter is unaffected by diaphragmatic contraction, which makes (d) wrong. Option (a) describes the caval opening, (c) gives the level of the oesophageal opening, and (e) describes the sphincteric action at the oesophageal opening.
questions.keyConcept: The aorta passes behind the median arcuate ligament, so diaphragmatic contraction does not compress it.
options: Dilates during inspiration to increase venous return.

questions.text: As regards the breast, choose the INCORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because this statement is incorrect: the breast extends vertically from the second to the sixth rib. The remaining statements are true, since the breast is a modified sweat gland of the skin (a), drains mainly to the axillary nodes (c), can spread across the midline through cutaneous lymphatics (d), and has a pigmented areola surrounding the nipple (e).
questions.keyConcept: The breast extends from the 2nd to the 6th rib and drains mainly to the axillary nodes.
options: It is a modified skin gland.
It extends between 3rd rib to 6th rib.
It drains its lymph into axillary lymph nodes.
Cancer of one side can cross to opposite side.

questions.text: All are true about breast except:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (D) because the breast extends vertically from the 2nd to the 6th rib, not to the 9th. The other statements are true: the breast is present in both sexes though rudimentary in the male, the pigmented skin around the nipple is the areola, and the axillary tail of Spence passes through the deep fascia to lie in the axilla.
questions.keyConcept: The breast extends from the 2nd to the 6th rib, and its axillary tail is a content of the axilla.
options: Both males and females have breast.
The dark pigmented area is named areola.
The tail is considered as content of axilla.
The lower boundary (Extent) of breast is 9th rib.
