questions.text: The deepest layer in the anterior abdominal wall is:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (D) because the parietal peritoneum is the innermost, and therefore deepest, layer of the anterior abdominal wall, lining the abdominal cavity itself. Working inwards the order is skin, Camper's fascia, Scarpa's fascia, the three muscle layers, fascia transversalis, extraperitoneal fat and finally peritoneum. Extraperitoneal fat (e) and fascia transversalis (c) are therefore both superficial to the peritoneum.
questions.keyConcept: The peritoneum is the deepest layer of the anterior abdominal wall.

questions.text: The anterior abdominal wall has the following arrangement from superficial to deep:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because transversus abdominis is the deepest of the three flat muscles, and it is followed inwards by fascia transversalis and then the parietal peritoneum. Option (a) is reversed because the fascial layers lie superficial to external oblique, and (c) and (e) list the layers from deep to superficial. Option (d) is wrong because internal oblique lies superficial to transversus abdominis, not deep to it.
questions.keyConcept: From superficial to deep the deep layers run transversus abdominis, fascia transversalis, then parietal peritoneum.
options: External oblique, Scarpa's fascia & Camper's fascia.
Transversus abdominis, Fascia transversalis & parietal peritoneum.
Fascia transversalis, transversus abdominis & internal oblique.
Scarpa's fascia, transversus abdominis & internal oblique.
Parietal peritoneum, fascia transversalis & transversus abdominis.

questions.text: Which structure lies immediately deep to the transversus abdominis muscle?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) because fascia transversalis is the layer immediately deep to transversus abdominis. Extraperitoneal fat (b) and parietal peritoneum (a) lie deeper still, so they are not the structure immediately deep to the muscle. Camper's and Scarpa's fasciae (d, e) are components of the superficial fascia and lie far superficial to the muscles.
questions.keyConcept: Fascia transversalis lies immediately deep to transversus abdominis.

questions.text: As regards the external oblique muscle, choose the CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (D) because the aponeurosis of external oblique reaches and is attached to the linea alba in the midline. Option (a) is wrong because it is the medial part of the muscle that becomes aponeurotic, and (b) is wrong because it is the lower border that rolls on itself to form the inguinal ligament. Option (c) is wrong because its fibers are directed downwards and forwards, and (e) is wrong because it is attached to ribs rather than to costal cartilages.
questions.keyConcept: External oblique fibers run downwards and forwards, become aponeurotic medially, and attach to the linea alba.
options: Its fibers are replaced laterally by an aponeurosis.
Its upper border forms the inguinal ligament.
Its fibers are directed downwards & backwards.
It is attached to linea alba.
It is attached to costal cartilages.

questions.text: As regards the internal oblique muscle, choose the INCORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) because this statement is incorrect: the fibers of internal oblique run upwards and forwards, in the opposite direction to those of external oblique, so that the two muscles cross at right angles. The remaining statements are true, since internal oblique is the middle of the three flat muscles (a), arises in part from the iliac crest (b), becomes aponeurotic medially (d) and reaches the linea alba (e).
questions.keyConcept: Internal oblique fibers run upwards, at right angles to the downward-and-forward fibers of external oblique.
options: It lies deep to external oblique.
Its fibers are attached to iliac crest.
Its fibers are directed downwards & forwards.
It is replaced medially by an aponeurosis.
It is attached to linea alba.

questions.text: As regards the internal oblique muscle, choose the CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because the fibers of internal oblique cross those of external oblique at a right angle, which is the basis of the strength of the abdominal wall. Option (a) is wrong because the fibers are directed upwards and medially, and (c) is wrong because the aponeurosis splits to enclose rectus abdominis, not transversus abdominis. Option (d) is wrong because it is the lower border that arches above the spermatic cord, and (e) is wrong because medially the muscle is aponeurotic rather than fleshy.
questions.keyConcept: The fibers of internal oblique cross those of external oblique at right angles.
options: Its fibers are directed upwards & laterally.
Its fibers in a right angle to fibers of external oblique.
Its aponeurosis splits to enclose transversus abdominis muscle.
Its upper border forms an arch above spermatic cord.
Medially, it is formed of fleshy fibers.

questions.text: As regards rectus abdominis muscle, choose the CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (A) because the two rectus abdominis muscles are strap muscles lying one on each side of the midline linea alba. Option (b) is wrong because it is attached below to the symphysis pubis, and (c) is wrong because its upper end is wide while its lower end is narrow. Option (d) is wrong because the lateral border forms the linea semilunaris, and (e) is wrong because it is divided by three transverse intersections.
questions.keyConcept: Rectus abdominis flanks the linea alba, is wide above and narrow below, and is crossed by three transverse tendinous intersections.
options: It lies on either side of linea alba.
It is attached above to symphysis pubis.
Its medial border forms linea semilunaris.
It is divided by 2 longitudinal intersections.

questions.text: As regards rectus abdominis muscle, choose INCORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (E) because this statement is incorrect: the lateral border of rectus abdominis forms the linea semilunaris, whereas the linea alba is the midline raphe between the two muscles. The remaining statements are true, since the muscle is enclosed in the aponeurotic rectus sheath (a, b), is narrow at its lower end (c), and is attached above to the 5th to 7th costal cartilages and the xiphoid process (d).
questions.keyConcept: The lateral border of rectus abdominis forms the linea semilunaris; the linea alba is in the midline.
options: It is enclosed within an aponeurosis.
It lies inside the rectus sheath.
Above, it is attached to ribs & sternum.
Its lateral border forms linea alba.

questions.text: As regards muscles of anterior abdominal wall, choose the CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because pyramidalis is a small, inconstant triangular muscle in front of the lower rectus abdominis and is frequently absent. Option (a) is wrong because it is rectus abdominis that lies within the rectus sheath, and (c) is wrong because external oblique arises from the lower 8 ribs. Option (d) is wrong because internal oblique fibers run upwards and medially, and (e) is wrong because rectus abdominis lies on each side of the linea alba.
questions.keyConcept: Pyramidalis is a small triangular muscle that may be absent.
options: Transversus abdominis is enclosed within rectus sheath.
External oblique is attached to lower 4 ribs.
Fibers of internal oblique are directed downwards & medially.
Rectus abdominis muscle lies on each side of linea semilunaris.

questions.text: Which one of the following muscles has its fibers directed upwards & forwards?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because internal oblique is the only flat muscle of the abdominal wall whose fibers are directed upwards and forwards. External oblique fibers (a) run in the opposite direction, downwards and forwards, and transversus abdominis fibers (c) run horizontally. Rectus abdominis (d) and pyramidalis (e) are vertical muscles.
questions.keyConcept: Internal oblique is the abdominal wall muscle whose fibers run upwards and forwards.

questions.text: Match each muscle in the left column with its appropriate description in the right column:
questions.explanation: Each muscle of the anterior abdominal wall has a signature feature. The rolled lower border of external oblique forms the inguinal ligament, internal oblique fibers run upwards and medially, and transversus abdominis fibers run horizontally and forwards. Rectus abdominis is crossed by three transverse tendinous intersections, and pyramidalis is the small triangular muscle in front of its lower part.
questions.keyConcept: External oblique forms the inguinal ligament, internal oblique runs upwards, transversus runs horizontally, rectus has 3 intersections, and pyramidalis is small and triangular.

pairs.target: Its lower border forms inguinal lig.
Its fibers are directed upwards & medially.

questions.text: As regards rectus sheath, choose INCORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (D) because this statement is incorrect: the posterior wall of the rectus sheath is formed by the aponeurosis of transversus abdominis together with the posterior lamella of the internal oblique aponeurosis, not by external oblique. The external oblique aponeurosis contributes only to the anterior wall (c). The remaining statements are true, since the sheath encloses rectus abdominis (a), is formed from all three flat muscle aponeuroses (b) and contains the superior and inferior epigastric arteries (e).
questions.keyConcept: The posterior wall of the rectus sheath is formed by transversus abdominis aponeurosis and the posterior lamella of internal oblique.
options: It is derived from aponeurosis of external oblique, internal oblique & transversus abdominis.
Its anterior wall is made by aponeurosis of external oblique & anterior lamella of internal oblique.
Its posterior wall is made by aponeurosis of external oblique & posterior lamella of internal oblique.

questions.text: Rectus sheath encloses all the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because transversus abdominis is one of the muscles whose aponeurosis helps to form the rectus sheath, so it lies outside the sheath rather than within it. The contents of the sheath are rectus abdominis and pyramidalis (a), the superior and inferior epigastric vessels (c, d) and the terminal parts of the lower intercostal nerves (e).
questions.keyConcept: Transversus abdominis forms the rectus sheath rather than lying inside it.

questions.text: As regards the inguinal canal, choose the CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) because the inguinal canal transmits the round ligament of the uterus in the female and the spermatic cord in the male. Option (a) is wrong because the canal lies above the inguinal ligament, and (b) is wrong because fascia transversalis lies in the posterior wall while external oblique forms the anterior wall. Option (d) is wrong because the canal is about 4 cm long, and (e) is wrong because the inguinal ligament forms its floor.
questions.keyConcept: The inguinal canal is about 4 cm long, lies above the inguinal ligament, and transmits the spermatic cord or the round ligament of the uterus.
options: It lies below the inguinal ligament.
Its anterior wall is formed by fascia transversalis.
It gives passage to round ligament of uterus.
Its roof is formed by inguinal ligament.

questions.text: As regards the inguinal canal, choose the INCORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The floor of the inguinal canal is formed by the inguinal ligament. The roof is formed by the arching fibers of internal oblique and transversus abdominis; the conjoint tendon reinforces the medial posterior wall rather than forming the roof.
questions.keyConcept: Inguinal canal roof = arching fibers of internal oblique and transversus abdominis; floor = inguinal ligament.
options: It gives passage to spermatic cord.
It extends between superficial & deep inguinal rings.
Its floor is formed by conjoint tendon.
Its anterior wall is formed by external oblique.
Its posterior wall is formed by fascia transversalis.

questions.text: Match each wall of inguinal canal in the left column with its forming structure in the right column:
questions.explanation: The anterior wall of the inguinal canal is formed mainly by the aponeurosis of external oblique, the posterior wall by fascia transversalis, the roof by the arching fibers of internal oblique and transversus abdominis, and the floor by the inguinal ligament.
questions.keyConcept: Inguinal canal boundaries: external oblique in front, fascia transversalis behind, arching fibers above, inguinal ligament below.

pairs.target: Arching fibers of internal oblique and transversus abdominis.

questions.text: Match each description in the left column with its name in the right column:
questions.explanation: The costal margin is formed by the cartilages of the lower ribs, and the xiphoid process is the small lowest part of the sternum. The linea alba is the vertical midline band formed by the interlacing aponeuroses of the flat abdominal muscles, running from the xiphoid process to the symphysis pubis. The umbilicus is a scar in the linea alba marking the site of the fetal umbilical cord.
questions.keyConcept: The linea alba is the midline aponeurotic band from xiphoid to symphysis pubis, and the umbilicus is a scar within it.

pairs.premise: Formed by aponeurosis of anterior abdominal muscles.
A vertical band between xiphoid process & symphysis pubis.

questions.text: Match each description in the left column with its name in the right column:
questions.explanation: The linea semilunaris is the curved lateral border of rectus abdominis, and it crosses the costal margin at the tip of the 9th costal cartilage. The iliac crest is the upper border of the ilium running between the anterior and posterior superior iliac spines, while the rolled lower border of external oblique forms the inguinal ligament. The symphysis pubis is the secondary cartilaginous joint uniting the two pubic bones in the midline.
questions.keyConcept: The linea semilunaris is the lateral border of rectus abdominis and crosses the costal margin at the 9th costal cartilage.

pairs.premise: Crosses costal margin at tip of 9th costal cartilage.
Lower border of external oblique ms.
Lateral border of rectus abdominis ms.

questions.text: Match each plane in the left column with its appropriate description in the right column:
questions.explanation: The intercristal plane joins the highest points of the two iliac crests and lies at the level of L4, which is why it is used as a landmark for lumbar puncture. The transpyloric plane passes through the tips of the 9th costal cartilages, and the intertubercular plane joins the tubercles of the iliac crests at the level of L5. The subcostal plane connects the lowest points of the costal margin, at the 10th costal cartilages.
questions.keyConcept: Intercristal plane is L4, intertubercular is L5, transpyloric crosses the 9th costal cartilages, and subcostal crosses the 10th.

pairs.target: Intersects with tip of 9th costal cart.
Connects 10th costal cartilages of both sides.

questions.text: The muscle attached to all lumbar vertebrae is:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (A) because psoas major arises from the bodies, transverse processes and intervertebral discs of all five lumbar vertebrae before descending to the lesser trochanter of the femur. Quadratus lumborum (c) is attached to the iliac crest and the last rib, with only limited vertebral attachment. Iliacus (e) arises from the iliac fossa and transversus abdominis (d) from the lumbar fascia.
questions.keyConcept: Psoas major arises from all five lumbar vertebrae and inserts into the lesser trochanter of the femur.

questions.text: Match each muscle in the left column with its appropriate attachment in the right column:
questions.explanation: Quadratus lumborum is a quadrilateral muscle stretching between the iliac crest below and the last rib above. Transversus abdominis arises posteriorly from the lumbar fascia and is inserted anteriorly into the linea alba. Psoas major runs from all the lumbar vertebrae to the femur, while iliacus arises from the iliac fossa and joins the psoas tendon to reach the femur, the two together forming iliopsoas.
questions.keyConcept: Quadratus lumborum spans iliac crest to last rib; psoas major and iliacus both reach the femur as iliopsoas.

questions.text: All the following nerves emerge from lateral side of psoas major EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) because the genitofemoral nerve is the one branch of the lumbar plexus that pierces psoas major and emerges on its anterior surface. The iliohypogastric, ilioinguinal, lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh and femoral nerve all appear at the lateral border of the muscle. The lumbosacral trunk and obturator nerve, by contrast, emerge from its medial border.
questions.keyConcept: The genitofemoral nerve emerges from the front of psoas major; most other lumbar plexus branches emerge laterally.

questions.text: All the following are branches of lumbar plexus EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (E) because the subcostal nerve is the ventral ramus of the 12th thoracic nerve and therefore belongs to the thoracic nerves, not to the lumbar plexus. The obturator, femoral, genitofemoral and lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh are all true branches of the lumbar plexus, which is formed from the ventral rami of L1 to L4. The plexus lies within the substance of psoas major.
questions.keyConcept: The subcostal nerve is the ventral ramus of T12 and is not a branch of the lumbar plexus.

questions.text: Which one of the following emerges from front of psoas major?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (D) because the genitofemoral nerve pierces the anterior surface of psoas major and descends on it before dividing into its genital and femoral branches. All the other nerves listed emerge at the lateral border of the muscle. This anterior course explains why the nerve is at risk in operations on the posterior abdominal wall.
questions.keyConcept: The genitofemoral nerve pierces psoas major and emerges on its anterior surface.

questions.text: Which one of the following emerges from medial side of psoas major?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (A) because the lumbosacral trunk emerges from the medial border of psoas major to descend into the pelvis and join the sacral plexus. The ilioinguinal nerve, lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh and femoral nerve all emerge from the lateral border. The genitofemoral nerve is exceptional in emerging from the anterior surface of the muscle.
questions.keyConcept: The lumbosacral trunk and obturator nerve emerge from the medial border of psoas major.

questions.text: Nerves of posterior abdominal wall include all the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because the lower intercostal nerves run in the neurovascular plane of the anterior abdominal wall rather than on the posterior abdominal wall. The subcostal nerve (a), the branches of the lumbar plexus such as the femoral and lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh (c, e), and the lumbar part of the sympathetic chain (d) all lie on the posterior abdominal wall.
questions.keyConcept: The lower intercostal nerves supply the anterior abdominal wall, not the posterior abdominal wall.

questions.text: As regards abdominal aorta, choose the CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (A) because the abdominal aorta terminates by dividing into the right and left common iliac arteries. Option (b) is wrong because this bifurcation occurs at the level of L4, and (c) is wrong because there is only one median sacral artery. Option (d) is wrong because the suprarenal arteries are paired, and (e) is wrong because the inferior mesenteric artery arises at the level of L3.
questions.keyConcept: The abdominal aorta ends at L4 by dividing into the two common iliac arteries.
options: It ends by giving 2 common iliac arteries.
It ends at level of L5.
It gives a pair of median sacral arteries.
It gives a single suprarenal artery.
It gives inferior mesenteric artery at level of L4.

questions.text: All the following are single branches of abdominal aorta EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because the phrenic arteries are paired, one passing to each half of the diaphragm. The three ventral visceral branches, namely the coeliac, superior mesenteric and inferior mesenteric arteries, are all single midline vessels, as is the median sacral artery. Paired branches supply the paired structures of the posterior abdominal wall and the retroperitoneum.
questions.keyConcept: Single aortic branches: coeliac, superior mesenteric, inferior mesenteric and median sacral. The phrenic arteries are paired.

questions.text: All the following are paired branches of abdominal aorta EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (D) because the coeliac artery is a single midline ventral branch that arises at the level of L1 and supplies the foregut. The common iliac, suprarenal, phrenic and renal arteries are all paired, arising as right and left vessels. The distinction between single and paired branches follows the midline versus bilateral arrangement of the structures they supply.
questions.keyConcept: The coeliac artery is a single ventral branch of the aorta; suprarenal, renal, phrenic and common iliac arteries are paired.

questions.text: Match each artery in the left column with its level of origin in the right column:
questions.explanation: The coeliac trunk arises at about L1, the renal arteries at about L2, the inferior mesenteric artery at about L3, and the aorta bifurcates into the common iliac arteries at L4. The gonadal arteries usually arise from the abdominal aorta around L2, typically just inferior to the renal arteries.
questions.keyConcept: Coeliac L1, renal L2, gonadal about L2, inferior mesenteric L3, aortic bifurcation L4.

questions.text: As regards inferior vena cava, choose the CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) because the inferior vena cava receives both the right and the left renal veins directly, the left being the longer as it crosses in front of the aorta. Option (a) is wrong because the cava begins at the level of L5 by the union of the two common iliac veins, and (b) is wrong because it ascends on the right side of the aorta. Option (d) is wrong because only the right gonadal vein drains into it, the left draining into the left renal vein, and (e) is wrong because it traverses the caval opening in the central tendon.
questions.keyConcept: The IVC begins at L5, ascends to the right of the aorta, and receives both renal veins but only the right gonadal vein.
options: It begins at level of L4.
It ascends on left side of aorta.
Ascends through esophageal opening of diaphragm.

questions.text: Inferior vena cava receives all the following veins EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) because the inferior vena cava receives the right suprarenal vein only, while the left suprarenal vein drains into the left renal vein. The renal veins (a), the hepatic veins (b), the right gonadal vein (d) and the common iliac veins (e) all drain directly into the cava. The left suprarenal and left gonadal veins share this same indirect route through the left renal vein.
questions.keyConcept: The IVC receives only the right suprarenal and right gonadal veins; the left ones drain into the left renal vein.

questions.text: Left gonadal vein ends in:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because the left gonadal vein ascends to drain at a right angle into the left renal vein, whereas the right gonadal vein drains directly into the inferior vena cava. This asymmetry produces a longer and more obstructed venous route on the left. It is the accepted anatomical explanation for the greater frequency of left-sided varicocele.
questions.keyConcept: The left gonadal vein drains into the left renal vein; the right drains directly into the IVC.

questions.text: Which of the following is retroperitoneal?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) because the duodenum, apart from its very first part, lies behind the peritoneum on the posterior abdominal wall and is therefore retroperitoneal. The liver, stomach, omenta and small intestine are all intraperitoneal, being invested by peritoneum and suspended by peritoneal folds. Retroperitoneal organs are covered by peritoneum on their anterior aspect only.
questions.keyConcept: The duodenum is retroperitoneal; the stomach, liver, omenta and small intestine are intraperitoneal.

questions.text: Which of the following is intraperitoneal?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (E) because the stomach is completely invested by peritoneum and is suspended by the greater and lesser omenta, which makes it intraperitoneal and mobile. The pancreas, ascending colon, kidney and suprarenal gland are all retroperitoneal and therefore relatively fixed. The peritoneal folds attached to intraperitoneal organs also carry their blood supply.
questions.keyConcept: The stomach is intraperitoneal and mobile; the pancreas, ascending colon, kidney and suprarenal gland are retroperitoneal.

questions.text: All the following are retroperitoneal structures EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (D) because the mesentery is itself a double-layered peritoneal fold, the structure that suspends the small intestine, and so it cannot be a retroperitoneal structure. The great vessels, the ureters, the descending colon and the duodenum all lie behind the peritoneum on the posterior abdominal wall. Peritoneal folds such as the mesentery belong to the intraperitoneal arrangement.
questions.keyConcept: The mesentery is a peritoneal fold, not a retroperitoneal structure.

questions.text: All the following are intraperitoneal structures EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) because the suprarenal gland lies on the upper pole of the kidney in the posterior retroperitoneal layer, behind the peritoneal sac. The omenta, intestine, liver and stomach are all intraperitoneal, being enclosed by peritoneum and connected to the wall by peritoneal folds. This retroperitoneal position is why the suprarenal gland is approached posteriorly in surgery.
questions.keyConcept: The suprarenal gland is retroperitoneal, lying with the kidney behind the peritoneal sac.

questions.text: As regards the retroperitoneal organs, choose the INCORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because this statement is incorrect: retroperitoneal organs are covered by peritoneum on their anterior aspect only, and it is intraperitoneal organs that are surrounded on all sides. The remaining statements are true, since these organs lie behind the peritoneal sac (a) on the posterior abdominal wall (e), with the kidneys in the posterior layer (c) and the duodenum in the anterior layer (d).
questions.keyConcept: Retroperitoneal organs are covered by peritoneum on their anterior aspect only.
options: They are surrounded all around by peritoneum.
They include kidneys which lie in posterior retroperitoneal layer.
They include duodenum which lies in anterior retroperitoneal layer.
They lie on posterior abdominal wall.

questions.text: Posterior retroperitoneal layer includes all the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (A) because the pancreas belongs to the anterior retroperitoneal layer, together with the duodenum and the ascending and descending colon. The posterior retroperitoneal layer contains the kidneys, ureters, suprarenal glands and the great vessels lying in front of the vertebral column. The distinction reflects the order in which these structures are encountered from front to back.
questions.keyConcept: The pancreas lies in the anterior retroperitoneal layer; the kidneys, ureters and great vessels lie in the posterior layer.

questions.text: Anterior retroperitoneal layer includes all the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (E) because the ureters descend with the kidneys in the posterior retroperitoneal layer, on the front of psoas major. The anterior retroperitoneal layer consists of the parts of the gut that have become secondarily fixed, namely the duodenum, pancreas, ascending colon and descending colon. Recognising these two layers helps predict what is encountered at successive depths on the posterior abdominal wall.
questions.keyConcept: The anterior retroperitoneal layer holds duodenum, pancreas and ascending and descending colon; the ureters lie in the posterior layer.

questions.text: As regards the posterior retroperitoneal layer, choose the INCORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because this statement is incorrect: the retroperitoneal parts of the gastrointestinal tract, namely the duodenum, pancreas and ascending and descending colon, all lie in the anterior retroperitoneal layer. The posterior layer is made up of urinary and endocrine organs and the great vessels, including the suprarenal glands (a), the aorta in front of the vertebral column (c) and the tributaries of the inferior vena cava (d). It is therefore the most posterior layer of abdominal organs (e).
questions.keyConcept: The posterior retroperitoneal layer contains urinary and vascular structures, not parts of the gut.
options: It includes the suprarenal glands on the sides.
It includes some organs of GIT.
It includes abdominal aorta infront of vertebral column.
It includes tributaries of inferior vena cava.
They form the most posterior layer of organs in abdomen.

questions.text: As regards the intraperitoneal organs, choose the CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (E) because the visceral peritoneum covering the organs becomes continuous with the parietal peritoneum lining the wall through double-layered peritoneal folds such as the mesentery and omenta. Option (a) is wrong because the organs invade the peritoneal cavity from behind, and (b) is wrong because intraperitoneal organs are completely covered. Options (c) and (d) reverse the two layers, since the visceral layer covers the organs and the parietal layer lines the abdominal wall.
questions.keyConcept: Peritoneal folds are double layers connecting the visceral peritoneum on the organs to the parietal peritoneum on the wall.
options: Its organs invade the peritoneal cavity from the front.
They are covered by peritoneum from front only.
Its visceral layer lines the abdominal wall.
Its parietal layer covers the organs.
Visceral & parietal layers are connected by peritoneal folds.

questions.text: As regards the intraperitoneal organs, choose the INCORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (D) because this statement is incorrect: the ascending colon is a retroperitoneal organ, covered by peritoneum on its anterior aspect only, and is not surrounded by a peritoneal fold. The remaining statements are true, since peritoneal folds are double-layered (a), carry the vessels and nerves of the organ between their layers (b), suspend the stomach as the omenta (c), and the small intestine is invested by visceral peritoneum (e).
questions.keyConcept: The ascending colon is retroperitoneal and has no suspending peritoneal fold.
options: Peritoneal folds enclose the blood supply of the organ.
Peritoneal folds surround the ascending colon.

questions.text: Match each organ in the left column with its related peritoneal fold in the right column:
questions.explanation: Peritoneal folds are named according to the organ they suspend. The stomach is suspended by the greater and lesser omenta, the small intestine by the mesentery, and the mobile parts of the large intestine by their mesocolons. The spleen and liver are attached by peritoneal ligaments, such as the gastrosplenic and lienorenal ligaments for the spleen and the falciform and coronary ligaments for the liver.
questions.keyConcept: Omenta suspend the stomach, the mesentery the small intestine, mesocolons the large intestine, and ligaments the liver and spleen.

questions.text: Right lobe of liver is suspended by:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) because the coronary ligament attaches the right lobe of the liver to the diaphragm, encircling the bare area. The falciform ligament (a) lies between the right and left lobes, and the left triangular ligament (b) anchors the left lobe. The lesser omentum (d) connects the liver to the stomach, while the greater omentum (e) has no attachment to the liver.
questions.keyConcept: The coronary ligament suspends the right lobe of the liver and surrounds its bare area.

questions.text: The peritoneal ligament that lies between right & left lobes of liver is:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (A) because the falciform ligament is the sickle-shaped double fold of peritoneum that runs on the diaphragmatic surface of the liver and marks the division between the right and left lobes. The triangular ligaments (b, c) anchor the extremities of the lobes to the diaphragm, and the coronary ligament (d) surrounds the bare area. The lesser omentum (e) passes from the liver to the lesser curvature of the stomach.
questions.keyConcept: The sickle-shaped falciform ligament separates the right and left lobes of the liver.

questions.text: The lesser omentum:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because the lesser omentum is the two-layered peritoneal fold that passes from the porta hepatis and fissure for the ligamentum venosum of the liver to the lesser curvature of the stomach. Option (a) is wrong because it attaches to the lesser and not the greater curvature. Options (c), (d) and (e) all describe the greater omentum, which is apron-shaped, folded upon itself and therefore composed of four layers.
questions.keyConcept: The lesser omentum is a two-layered fold from the liver to the lesser curvature of the stomach.
options: Is attached to greater curvature of stomach.

questions.text: As regards the peritoneal folds of the stomach, choose the CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (E) because the greater omentum descends from the greater curvature as a two-layered apron and then folds back on itself, so that it is composed of four layers. Options (a), (c) and (d) wrongly attribute the characters of the greater omentum to the lesser omentum, which is a simple two-layered fold. Option (b) is wrong because the lesser omentum is attached to the lesser curvature.
questions.keyConcept: The greater omentum is folded upon itself and so consists of four layers of peritoneum.
options: Its lesser omentum has 2 anterior layers & 2 posterior layers.
Its lesser omentum is attached to its greater curvature.
Its lesser omentum is folded upon itself.
Its lesser omentum connects stomach with posterior abdominal wall.
Its greater omentum is formed of 4 layers.

questions.text: As regards the greater omentum, choose the INCORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because this statement is incorrect: the spleen is attached to the left convexity of the greater omentum, in keeping with its position in the left hypochondrium. The remaining statements are true, since the greater omentum runs from the greater curvature to the posterior abdominal wall (a), and the spleen splits its left extremity into the gastrosplenic ligament from the anterior two layers and the lienorenal ligament from the posterior two layers (c, d, e).
questions.keyConcept: The spleen is attached to the left convexity of the greater omentum, splitting it into gastrosplenic and lienorenal ligaments.
options: It connects greater curvature of stomach with post. abdominal wall.
Spleen is attached to its right convexity.
Lienorenal ligament is continuous with its posterior 2 layers.
Gastrosplenic ligament is continuous with its anterior 2 layers.
Spleen divides it into gastrosplenic & lienorenal ligaments.

questions.text: As regards the peritoneal cavity, choose the INCORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (E) because this statement is incorrect: the epiploic foramen of Winslow lies behind the free right border of the lesser omentum, which contains the portal triad. The remaining statements are true, since the stomach and omenta partition the cavity into a greater and a lesser sac (a), the greater sac lies in front of the stomach (b), the lesser sac behind it (c), and the two communicate through the epiploic foramen (d).
questions.keyConcept: The epiploic foramen lies behind the free right border of the lesser omentum.
options: Stomach & omenta divide it into greater & lesser sacs.
Its greater sac lies infront of stomach.
Its lesser sac lies behind stomach.
Both sacs are continuous through epiploic foramen.
Epiploic foramen lies behind free border of greater omentum.

questions.text: As regards the transverse colon, choose INCORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because this statement is incorrect: the transverse mesocolon is adherent to the posterior two layers of the greater omentum, not the anterior two. The remaining statements are true, since the transverse colon is exposed by reflecting the greater omentum upwards (a), lies at the level of the pancreas (c), is suspended by the transverse mesocolon from the posterior abdominal wall (d), and that mesocolon can be separated surgically from the omentum (e).
questions.keyConcept: The transverse mesocolon is adherent to the posterior two layers of the greater omentum.
options: It is seen on reflecting greater omentum upwards.
Its peritoneal fold is adherent to anterior 2 layers of greater omentum.
It lies at level of pancreas.
Its mesocolon suspends it to posterior abdominal wall.
Its mesocolon is separatable from greater omentum.

questions.text: Which one of the following peritoneal folds is located in the left side of the abdomen?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) because the sigmoid mesocolon suspends the sigmoid or pelvic colon, which lies in the left iliac fossa and pelvis. The mesoappendix (b) is on the right side with the caecum, and the mesentery (a) and transverse mesocolon (d) are largely midline structures. The falciform ligament (e) lies in the median plane of the upper abdomen.
questions.keyConcept: The sigmoid mesocolon is the peritoneal fold of the left side of the abdomen.

questions.text: As regards liver, choose the CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because the liver lies high under the diaphragm and is almost entirely concealed behind the lower ribs and costal cartilages, which is why it is not normally palpable in health. Option (a) is wrong because it lies mainly in the right hypochondrium, and (c) is wrong because it is wedge-shaped. Option (d) is wrong because its apex points to the left, and (e) is wrong because it lies above the subcostal plane.
questions.keyConcept: The liver is a wedge-shaped organ of the right hypochondrium, hidden behind the thoracic cage.
options: It lies mainly in left hypochondrium.
It is hidden by thoracic cage.
Its apex is directed to the right.

questions.text: The peritoneal fold that is attached between right & left lobes of liver:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (D) because the fold between the right and left lobes is the falciform ligament, whose name means sickle-shaped. Option (a) is wrong because the ligamentum venosum is the fibrous remnant of the ductus venosus and not a peritoneal fold, and (b) and (c) are wrong because the falciform ligament is attached to the diaphragmatic and not the visceral surface. Option (e) is wrong because the bare area is encircled by the coronary ligament.
questions.keyConcept: The falciform ligament is the sickle-shaped fold on the diaphragmatic surface between the two lobes of the liver.

questions.text: The visceral aspect of the liver shows all the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) because the falciform ligament is attached to the diaphragmatic aspect of the liver, not to its visceral surface. The visceral surface bears the H-shaped set of grooves formed by the groove for the inferior vena cava (a), the fissures for the ligamentum teres and ligamentum venosum (b, e) and the fossa for the gall bladder (d). The horizontal bar of this H is the porta hepatis.
questions.keyConcept: The visceral surface of the liver bears an H-shaped arrangement of grooves; the falciform ligament attaches to the diaphragmatic surface.

questions.text: The area which serves as entrance to & exit from liver is called:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (D) because the porta hepatis is the transverse fissure on the visceral surface through which the portal vein and hepatic artery enter and the hepatic ducts leave the liver. The caudate and quadrate lobes (a, e) are areas of liver substance bounded by these grooves, not gateways. The fissures for the ligamentum teres and ligamentum venosum (b, c) contain fibrous remnants of fetal vessels.
questions.keyConcept: The porta hepatis transmits the portal vein, hepatic artery and hepatic ducts.

questions.text: The horizontal link in the H-shaped groove on visceral aspect of liver is formed by:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (D) because the porta hepatis forms the transverse limb that links the two vertical limbs of the H-shaped groove. The right vertical limb is formed by the groove for the inferior vena cava and the fossa for the gall bladder, and the left by the fissures for the ligamentum venosum and ligamentum teres. The caudate and quadrate lobes are the areas of liver enclosed within this H.
questions.keyConcept: The porta hepatis is the horizontal bar of the H-shaped groove on the visceral surface of the liver.

questions.text: The bare area is a part of:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (A) because the bare area is the triangular part of the posterior surface of the right lobe that is devoid of peritoneum and rests directly against the diaphragm. It is bounded by the two layers of the coronary ligament, and the inferior vena cava lies in a groove at its left limit. The caudate and quadrate lobes (d, e) are on the visceral surface and are peritonealised.
questions.keyConcept: The bare area is the non-peritonealised part of the posterior surface of the right lobe of the liver.

questions.text: As regards the stomach ends, choose the CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because the cardiac end is the junction between the oesophagus and the stomach, situated behind the 7th left costal cartilage. Option (a) is wrong because the cardiac sphincter is physiological rather than anatomical, and (c) is wrong because it lies within the fibers of the right crus of the diaphragm. Option (d) is wrong because the pyloric sphincter is a strong anatomical sphincter, and (e) is wrong because the pyloric end opens into the duodenum.
questions.keyConcept: The cardiac sphincter is physiological, the pyloric sphincter anatomical, and the pylorus opens into the duodenum.
options: Its cardiac end has a strong anatomical sphincter.
It cardiac end lies between stomach & esophagus.
Its cardiac end lies within the fibers of left crus of diaphragm.
Its pyloric end has a thin sphincter.
Its pyloric end lies between stomach & jejunum.

questions.text: Gastrosplenic ligament is attached to:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (D) because the gastrosplenic ligament passes from the greater curvature of the stomach to the hilum of the spleen, being derived from the anterior two layers of the greater omentum. The lesser curvature (c) gives attachment instead to the lesser omentum. The ligament transmits the short gastric and left gastroepiploic vessels.
questions.keyConcept: The gastrosplenic ligament runs from the greater curvature of the stomach to the hilum of the spleen.

questions.text: As regards the stomach, choose the CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because the pyloric antrum is the funnel-shaped part of the pyloric portion of the stomach, leading from the body to the narrow pyloric canal. Option (a) is wrong because the fundus rises above the level of the cardiac orifice, and (c) is wrong because the pyloric canal lies distal to the body. Option (d) is wrong because the body lies before that imaginary line, and (e) is wrong because it is the fundus that usually contains the gastric air bubble.
questions.keyConcept: The pyloric antrum is funnel-shaped, and the gastric air bubble collects in the fundus.
options: Its fundus lies below the level of the cardiac end.
Its pyloric canal lies between fundus & body.
Its body lies after its imaginary line between notch on lesser curvature & bulge of greater curvature opposite it.
Its body usually contains an air bubble.

questions.text: Large intestine includes all the following parts EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (E) because the duodenum is the first part of the small intestine, not of the large intestine. The large intestine extends from the caecum with its appendix, through the ascending colon, hepatic flexure, transverse colon, splenic flexure, descending colon and sigmoid colon, to the rectum and anal canal. Its distinguishing features are the taeniae coli, sacculations and appendices epiploicae.
questions.keyConcept: The duodenum belongs to the small intestine; the large intestine runs from caecum to anal canal.

questions.text: Which order of arrangement of large intestine is CORRECT?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) because the proper sequence is caecum, ascending colon, hepatic flexure, transverse colon, splenic flexure, descending colon, sigmoid colon, rectum and anal canal, and option (c) lists four of these in their true relative order. Options (a), (b) and (d) place the ascending or transverse colon out of sequence, and (e) reverses the whole course. Tracing the gut in order from the ileocaecal junction distally is the safest way to answer such questions.
questions.keyConcept: Large intestine order: caecum, ascending colon, hepatic flexure, transverse colon, splenic flexure, descending colon, sigmoid colon, rectum, anal canal.
options: Hepatic flexure - transverse colon - ascending colon - descending colon.
Caecum - ascending colon - descending colon - transverse colon.
Caecum - hepatic flexure - sigmoid colon - rectum.
Splenic flexure - transverse colon - ascending colon - sigmoid colon.
Sigmoid colon - splenic flexure - hepatic flexure - caecum.

questions.text: Which of the following is a mobile organ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (E) because the pelvic or sigmoid colon is suspended by the sigmoid mesocolon and is therefore intraperitoneal and mobile. The ascending and descending colon and the two colic flexures are secondarily retroperitoneal and thus fixed to the posterior abdominal wall. This mobility explains why the sigmoid colon is the commonest site of colonic volvulus.
questions.keyConcept: The pelvic (sigmoid) colon has a mesocolon and is mobile; the ascending and descending colon are fixed.

questions.text: As regards large intestine, choose the INCORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (D) because this statement is incorrect: the wall of the large intestine carries three longitudinal bands of taeniae coli, formed by the condensed outer longitudinal muscle. The remaining statements are true, since it begins as the caecum (a), measures about one and a half metres (b), frames the coils of small intestine (c) and bears fatty appendices epiploicae (e).
questions.keyConcept: The large intestine has three taeniae coli, plus sacculations and appendices epiploicae.
options: It surrounds coils of small intestine.
Its walls has 2 long bands of taenia coli.

questions.text: As regards the duodenum, choose the CORRECT statement:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (D) because the duodenum is a C-shaped tube whose concavity clasps the head of the pancreas. Option (a) is wrong because it is formed of four parts, and (b) is wrong because it is retroperitoneal apart from its first part. Option (c) is wrong because its second part is about 3 inches long, and (e) is wrong because the whole duodenum measures about 25 cm, that is 10 inches.
questions.keyConcept: The duodenum has four parts, is retroperitoneal, is about 25 cm long, and encircles the head of the pancreas.

questions.text: Regarding to abdominal organs all the following organs are retroperitoneal except:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) because the spleen is completely intraperitoneal, suspended by the gastrosplenic and splenorenal ligaments. The duodenum apart from its first inch, the ascending colon and the pancreas apart from its tail are all retroperitoneal structures on the posterior abdominal wall.
questions.keyConcept: The spleen is intraperitoneal; the duodenum, ascending colon and pancreas are retroperitoneal.

questions.text: Subcostal plane opposite to all the following levels except:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (D) because the subcostal plane lies at the level of the third lumbar vertebra, not the fifth. It passes through the lowest point of the costal margin, formed by the tenth costal cartilage on each side, which is exactly what options (a), (b) and (c) describe.
questions.keyConcept: The subcostal plane passes through the 10th costal cartilages at the level of L3.

questions.text: Neuro vascular plane of the ant abdominal wall located between which of the following pairs?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) because the lower intercostal and subcostal nerves and vessels run forwards in the plane between the internal oblique and the transversus abdominis, which is the abdominal continuation of the thoracic neurovascular plane. This is the plane used for a transversus abdominis plane block.
questions.keyConcept: The abdominal neurovascular plane lies between internal oblique and transversus abdominis.

questions.text: All are true about duodenum except:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) because the vertical (second, descending) part of the duodenum measures three inches, not two; the classical lengths are 2, 3, 4 and 1 inches for the four parts. The remaining statements are true, since the duodenum apart from its first inch is retroperitoneal, its concavity embraces the head of the pancreas, and the third part crosses in front of the third lumbar vertebra.
questions.keyConcept: Duodenal parts measure 2, 3, 4 and 1 inches; the third part crosses L3.
options: It is a retro peritoneal in position.
The 3rd part opposite to 3rd lumbar vertebrae.

questions.text: Liver occupies all the following areas except:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because the liver never reaches the hypogastrium, the lowest median region of the abdomen. It occupies the right hypochondrium and epigastrium and extends into the left hypochondrium as far as the left lateral line.
questions.keyConcept: The liver occupies the right hypochondrium, epigastrium and part of the left hypochondrium.

questions.text: Bare area of liver located on which surface?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (D) because the bare area lies on the posterior surface of the right lobe, where the liver is in direct contact with the diaphragm without any intervening peritoneum, bounded by the reflections of the coronary ligament. The anterior, right and inferior surfaces are all covered by peritoneum apart from the fossae for the gallbladder and porta hepatis.
questions.keyConcept: The bare area of the liver lies on its posterior surface, in direct contact with the diaphragm.

questions.text: All the following structures are completely intra peritoneal except:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) because the descending colon is retroperitoneal, lying on the posterior abdominal wall with peritoneum covering only its anterior and lateral surfaces. The appendix has a mesoappendix, the jejunum a mesentery, and the spleen its own peritoneal ligaments, so all three are completely intraperitoneal.
questions.keyConcept: Ascending and descending colon are retroperitoneal; the appendix, jejunum and spleen are intraperitoneal.

questions.text: Which of the following peritoneal folds are attached to lesser curvature of the stomach?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because the lesser omentum passes from the lesser curvature of the stomach and the first inch of the duodenum to the porta hepatis and the fissure for the ligamentum venosum. The greater omentum and the gastrosplenic ligament are attached to the greater curvature, while the splenorenal ligament runs from the spleen to the posterior abdominal wall.
questions.keyConcept: The lesser omentum joins the lesser curvature of the stomach to the liver.

questions.text: Abdominal part of I.V.C begins at which level?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (A) because the inferior vena cava is formed at the level of the fifth lumbar vertebra by the union of the two common iliac veins, a little below and to the right of the aortic bifurcation. It then ascends to pierce the diaphragm at T8.
questions.keyConcept: The IVC begins at L5 from the union of the common iliac veins and pierces the diaphragm at T8.

questions.text: All of the following muscles shares in the post abdominal wall except:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) because the internal oblique is one of the three flat muscles of the anterolateral abdominal wall, not of the posterior wall. The posterior abdominal wall is formed by psoas major, quadratus lumborum and iliacus, together with the diaphragm above.
questions.keyConcept: Posterior abdominal wall muscles: psoas major, quadratus lumborum and iliacus.

questions.text: All of the following branches from abdominal aorta at level of (L1) except:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because the gonadal (testicular or ovarian) artery arises lower down, at the level of the second lumbar vertebra. The coeliac trunk arises at the T12/L1 level and the superior mesenteric and middle suprarenal arteries at L1.
questions.keyConcept: L1: coeliac trunk, superior mesenteric and suprarenal arteries. The gonadal artery arises at L2.

questions.text: Which of the following nerves related to medial border of psoas major?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because the obturator nerve emerges from the medial border of psoas major to run along the lateral pelvic wall towards the obturator canal. The genitofemoral nerve pierces the anterior surface of the muscle, while the iliohypogastric, ilioinguinal and lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh appear at its lateral border.
questions.keyConcept: Obturator nerve: medial border of psoas. Genitofemoral: anterior surface. The rest: lateral border.

questions.text: All are true about inguinal canal except:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) because the roof of the inguinal canal is formed by the arching lowest fibers of internal oblique and transversus abdominis; the fascia transversalis forms the posterior wall, not the roof. The remaining statements are true, since the superficial ring is a defect in the external oblique aponeurosis, the floor is the grooved upper surface of the inguinal ligament, and the anterior wall is the external oblique aponeurosis throughout.
questions.keyConcept: Inguinal canal: anterior wall external oblique, floor inguinal ligament, roof arching internal oblique and transversus, posterior wall fascia transversalis.
options: Its superficial ring in ext. oblique aponeurosis.
The roof is by fascia transversalis.
The floor is formed by inguinal ligament.
The ant wall is by ext. oblique.

questions.text: The neurovascular plane of the anterior abdominal wall lies between:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Internal oblique and transversus abdominis muscles. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: Internal oblique and transversus abdominis muscles
options: Superficial fascia and external oblique muscle
External oblique and internal oblique muscles
Internal oblique and transversus abdominis muscles
Transversus abdominis muscle and fascia transversalis

questions.text: The inguinal ligament is the lower border of which muscle?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is External oblique. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: External oblique

questions.text: The conjoint tendon is formed by the lower borders of which muscles?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Internal oblique and transversus abdominis. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: Internal oblique and transversus abdominis

questions.text: A cut wound reaching the rectus sheath will not affect:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Upper 6 intercostal nerves. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: Upper 6 intercostal nerves

questions.text: The deep inguinal ring is an opening in:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Fascia transversalis. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: Fascia transversalis

questions.text: The highest points on the iliac crests lie at the level of which vertebra?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is L4. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: The correct answer is L4. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification

questions.text: A muscle which may be absent is:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Psoas minor. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: The correct answer is Psoas minor. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification

questions.text: All the following nerves lie lateral to the psoas major muscle EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Obturator. The remaining options describe the normal anatomy correctly.
questions.keyConcept: The correct answer is Obturator. The remaining options describe the normal anatomy correctly

questions.text: The abdominal aorta ends at the lower border of which vertebra?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is L4. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: The correct answer is L4. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification

questions.text: The inferior vena cava receives all the following tributaries EXCEPT the:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Left gonadal vein. The remaining options describe the normal anatomy correctly.
questions.keyConcept: Left gonadal vein

questions.text: Which of the following organs is retroperitoneal?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Pancreas. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: The correct answer is Pancreas. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification

questions.text: The peritoneal fold of the small intestine is called:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Mesentery. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: The correct answer is Mesentery. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification

questions.text: The structure that suspends the lesser curvature of the stomach to the liver is the:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Lesser omentum. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: Lesser omentum

questions.text: The gall bladder is attached to which surface of the liver?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Inferior. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: The correct answer is Inferior. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification

questions.text: All the following are true about the stomach EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Both cardiac end and pyloric end have thick muscular sphincter. The remaining options describe the normal anatomy correctly.
questions.keyConcept: Both cardiac end and pyloric end have thick muscular sphincter
options: It has fundus, body and pylorus
Both cardiac end and pyloric end have thick muscular sphincter
Lesser curvature gives attachment to lesser omentum
Greater curvature gives attachment to greater omentum

questions.text: The vermiform appendix is attached to:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Cecum. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: The correct answer is Cecum. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification

questions.text: The kidney extends between which vertebral levels?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is T12–L3. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification.
questions.keyConcept: The correct answer is T12–L3. The remaining options do not fit the same anatomical relationship or classification

questions.text: The circulation that begins from capillaries and ends into capillaries:
questions.explanation: A portal system connects two capillary beds in series.
questions.keyConcept: Portal Circulation: A portal system connects two capillary beds in series

questions.text: Which of the following circulations connects two sets of blood capillaries?
questions.explanation: Portal circulation carries blood from one capillary bed to another capillary bed.
questions.keyConcept: Portal system

questions.text: The following are parts of alimentary tract, except:
questions.explanation: The liver is an accessory digestive organ, not a segment of the alimentary tract.
questions.keyConcept: The liver is an accessory organ, not part of the alimentary tract.

questions.text: All The following structures are related to the stomach bed, except:
questions.explanation: The liver is mainly an anterior relation of the stomach, not a component of the stomach bed.
questions.keyConcept: The liver is not part of the stomach bed.

questions.text: Regarding the duodenum one of the following statements is true;
questions.explanation: The common bile duct opens into the second part of the duodenum at the major duodenal papilla, usually together with the main pancreatic duct.
questions.keyConcept: The second part of the duodenum receives the common bile duct at the major duodenal papilla.
options: It is the longest part of small intestine.
It extends from the pylorus to the iliocaecal junction.
It is the middle part of small intestine.
Its length is about three meters.
Its second part receives the opening of the common bile duct.

questions.text: The following are parts of the large intestine, except:
questions.explanation: The oesophagus is not part of the large intestine.
questions.keyConcept: The oesophagus is not a component of the large intestine.

questions.text: The commonest position of the human appendix is:
questions.explanation: The retrocaecal position is the commonest position of the appendix.
questions.keyConcept: Retrocaecal is the commonest appendix position.

questions.text: The porta hepatis contains all the following structures, except:
questions.explanation: The coeliac artery itself does not pass through the porta hepatis.
questions.keyConcept: The porta hepatis does not contain the coeliac artery.

questions.text: Regarding the common bile duct one of the following statements is true;
questions.explanation: The common bile duct joins the main pancreatic duct to form the hepatopancreatic ampulla.
questions.keyConcept: The common bile duct joins the pancreatic duct at the ampulla of Vater.
options: Its Dimensions are 3.5 cm long and 20 mm in diameter.
Its Beginning is formed by the union of cystic duct and right hepatic duct.
It descends behind the fourth part of duodenum then behind the head of pancreas.
It unites with the pancreatic duct to form the hepato-pancreatic duct (ampulla of vater).
The ampulla opens at the middle of the jejunum.

questions.text: The stomach has two orifices ___ and ___.
questions.explanation: The stomach has a cardiac inlet and a pyloric outlet.
questions.keyConcept: The stomach has cardiac and pyloric orifices.

questions.text: Liver is related to ___ surface of the stomach while the pancreas is related to ___ surface.
questions.explanation: The liver is an anterior relation of the stomach, while the pancreas is a posterior relation.
questions.keyConcept: The liver is anterior to the stomach; the pancreas is posterior.

questions.text: Parts of the stomach are ___, ___ and ___.
questions.explanation: The stomach is described here as fundus, body, and pyloric part.
questions.keyConcept: Stomach parts include fundus, body, and pyloric part.

questions.text: Branches of the ___ artery form the arterial supply of the stomach.
questions.explanation: The stomach is supplied by branches of the coeliac trunk.
questions.keyConcept: Stomach Blood Supply: The stomach is supplied by branches of the coeliac trunk

questions.text: The small intestine is formed of ___, ___ and ileum.
questions.explanation: The small intestine consists of duodenum, jejunum, and ileum.
questions.keyConcept: Small intestine = duodenum, jejunum, and ileum.

questions.text: The Caecum communicates superiorly with ___ and medially with ___.
questions.explanation: The caecum continues superiorly as ascending colon and receives the ileum medially.
questions.keyConcept: The caecum communicates with ascending colon and ileum.

questions.text: The commonest position of the appendix is ___.
questions.explanation: The retrocaecal position is the commonest position of the appendix.
questions.keyConcept: The commonest appendix position is retrocaecal.

questions.text: Cystic duct joins ___ duct to form ___ duct.
questions.explanation: The cystic duct joins the common hepatic duct to form the common bile duct.
questions.keyConcept: Cystic duct + common hepatic duct = common bile duct.

questions.text: The common bile duct terminates in ___ part of the duodenum.
questions.explanation: The common bile duct opens into the second part of the duodenum.
questions.keyConcept: Common Bile Duct: The common bile duct opens into the second part of the duodenum
